require "fpm/package"
require "fpm/errors"
require "backports/latest"

# Empty Package type. For strict/meta/virtual package creation

class FPM::Package::Empty < FPM::Package
  def output(output_path)
    logger.warn("Your package has gone into the void.")
  end
  def to_s(fmt)
    return ""
  end

  def validate(validator)
    command = validator.instance_variable_get(:@command)
    messages = validator.messages
    channel = validator.logger

    input_opt = command.class.declared_options.find do |opt|
      opt.attribute_name == "input_type"
    end
    output_opt = command.class.declared_options.find do |opt|
      opt.attribute_name == "output_type"
    end

    input_type = command.input_type
    output_type = command.output_type
    args = command.args

    channel.debug("Validating command flags",
                  :architecture => @architecture,
                  :level => channel.level,
                  :input_flag => input_opt.attribute_name,
                  :output_flag => output_opt.attribute_name)

    mark_invalid = lambda do |value, error|
      if value.nil? or !value
        messages << error.message
        validator.instance_variable_set(:@valid, false)
      end
    end

    mark_invalid.call(input_type,
                      FPM::Package::InvalidArgument.new(
                        "Missing required -s flag. What package source did you want?"))
    mark_invalid.call(output_type,
                      FPM::Package::InvalidArgument.new(
                        "Missing required -t flag. What package output did you want?"))

    types = FPM::Package.types.keys.sort
    unless input_type.nil?
      mark_invalid.call(FPM::Package.types.include?(input_type),
                        FPM::InvalidPackageConfiguration.new(
                          "Invalid input package -s flag) type #{input_type.inspect}. " \
                          "Expected one of: #{types.join(", ")}"))
    end

    unless output_type.nil?
      mark_invalid.call(FPM::Package.types.include?(output_type),
                        FPM::InvalidPackageConfiguration.new(
                          "Invalid output package (-t flag) type #{output_type.inspect}. " \
                          "Expected one of: #{types.join(", ")}"))
    end

    command.dependencies.each do |dep|
      next unless dep.include?(",")
      splitdeps = dep.split(/\s*,\s*/)
      messages << "Dependencies should not " \
        "include commas. If you want to specify multiple dependencies, use " \
        "the '-d' flag multiple times. Example: " + \
        splitdeps.map { |d| "-d '#{d}'" }.join(" ")
    end

    if command.inputs
      mark_invalid.call(input_type == "dir",
                        FPM::InvalidPackageConfiguration.new(
                          "--inputs is only valid with -s dir"))
    end

    mark_invalid.call(args.any? || command.inputs || input_type == 'empty',
                      FPM::Package::InvalidArgument.new(
                        "No parameters given. You need to pass additional command " \
                        "arguments so that I know what you want to build packages " \
                        "from. For example, for '-s dir' you would pass a list of " \
                        "files and directories. For '-s gem' you would pass a one" \
                        " or more gems to package from. As a full example, this " \
                        "will make an rpm of the 'json' rubygem: " \
                        "`fpm -s gem -t rpm json`"))
  end
end

      subject.architecture = "native"

require "socket"
      # In 2019, Ruby's FileUtils added this as a way to "copy" a unix socket.
      # Reference: https://github.com/ruby/fileutils/pull/36/files
      UNIXServer.new(dst).close()
    when 'characterSpecial', 'blockSpecial'
      raise  UnsupportedSpecialFile.new("File is device which fpm doesn't know how to copy (#{File.ftype(src)}): #{src}")
    when 'directory'
      FileUtils.mkdir(dst) unless File.exists? dst
    else
      # if the file with the same dev and inode has been copied already -
      # hard link it's copy to `dst`, otherwise make an actual copy
      st = File.lstat(src)
      known_entry = copied_entries[[st.dev, st.ino]]
      if known_entry

Done. Summary of changes:

**Core fix** (the issue): `lib/fpm/package/empty.rb:8` — `FPM::Package::Empty#initialize` now sets `@architecture = "all"` after calling super, since empty packages have no files and aren't architecture-specific. An explicit `-a native` (or any `--architecture`) still overrides it, and output types translate it properly (`deb` → `all`, `rpm` → `noarch`).

**Required compat fixes** (pre-existing Ruby 3.3 breakage that made the CLI and several specs fail even before this change): replaced removed `File.exists?` with `File.exist?` in `lib/fpm/command.rb`, `lib/fpm/util.rb`, `lib/fpm/package/{deb,dir,puppet}.rb`.
